knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5

library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Gearhart_1994_dfp_mouse_pbpk"))$reference`
* Article: [Environ Health Perspect 1994;102(Suppl 11):51-60](https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.94102s1151)

Gearhart et al. 1994 developed a physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK)
model for diisopropylfluorophosphate (DFP, an organophosphate ester and a
cholinesterase-inhibitor tool compound) coupled to a mechanistic model of
acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibition, for organophosphate risk assessment.
The same structure was parameterised for three species; this package ships one
model file per species:

```{r models}
mouse <- readModelDb("Gearhart_1994_dfp_mouse_pbpk")
rat <- readModelDb("Gearhart_1994_dfp_rat_pbpk")
human <- readModelDb("Gearhart_1994_dfp_human_pbpk")
mUi <- rxode2::rxode2(mouse)
rUi <- rxode2::rxode2(rat)
hUi <- rxode2::rxode2(human)
```

# Model structure and population

DFP disposition is a flow-limited whole-body PBPK: brain, liver, kidney and
richly perfused tissue are flow-limited with saturable A-esterase (DFPase)
hydrolysis (Michaelis-Menten); fat, slowly perfused tissue and diaphragm are
flow-limited storage; venous and arterial blood are explicit compartments that
also hydrolyse DFP, because blood A-esterase strongly limits the amount of DFP
reaching target tissue (Discussion). The lung is an algebraic steady-state gas
exchanger coupling cardiac output and alveolar ventilation through the blood:air
partition, so inhalation can enter as an air concentration while iv and sc/im
doses enter as dose records (Appendix II; Figure 1).

AChE in brain and in blood is tracked as a free/inhibited/aged pool (Figure 2):
free (active) enzyme is irreversibly inhibited by local DFP at a bimolecular
rate; inhibited enzyme either regenerates to the active form or ages to a
permanently inactive form; and the free pool turns over by zero-order synthesis
balanced against first-order degradation. The readout is enzyme activity as a
fraction of the pre-exposure control. The model is deterministic: the
publication reports no between-subject variability and no residual error.

The three parameterisations cover (Table 4):

```{r population}
mouse()$population$species
rat()$population$species
human()$population$species
```

The in vitro DFP tissue:blood partition coefficients, A-esterase hydrolysis
Vmax/Km and the AChE bimolecular inhibition rate were measured in male
Fischer-344 rat tissue homogenates; mouse and human Vmax values were scaled from
the rat by body weight^0.7 and the rat Km used directly (Methods; Tables 1, 5).

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its table in the
source. The full text of this paper is distributed as scanned page images, so
the tabulated values were read directly from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 of the
scanned article. Representative entries (mouse file):

| Equation / parameter | Value (mouse) | Source location |
|----------------------|---------------|-----------------|
| Blood:air partition `pc_blood_air` | 12.57 | Table 5, DFP blood-air |
| Fat:blood partition `pc_fat` | 17.6 | Table 5, DFP fat-blood |
| Venous-blood DFPase `vmax_venous` / `km_venous` | 79.38 mg/h / 198.7 mg/L | Table 1, Venous blood, mouse |
| Liver DFPase `vmax_liver` / `km_liver` | 256.58 mg/h / 237.36 mg/L | Table 1, Liver, mouse |
| AChE inhibition `ki` | 14.16 1/uM/h | Table 1 / Table 3, AChE |
| AChE regeneration `kreg` | 0.016 1/h | Table 3, Enzyme regeneration |
| AChE aging `kage` | 0.297 1/h (mouse) | Table 3, Enzyme aging |
| AChE degradation brain `kdeg_brain` | 0.010 1/h | Table 3, Enzyme degradation, Brain |
| AChE degradation plasma `kdeg_plasma` | 0.060 1/h (mouse) | Table 3, Enzyme degradation, Plasma |
| Cardiac output `qc` | 1.04 L/h (mouse) | Table 4, Cardiac output |
| DFP mass-balance ODE (tissue) | n/a | Appendix II, `VT dCT/dt = QT(CAB - CT/PT)` |
| DFP hydrolysis term | n/a | Appendix II, `Vmax*CV/(Km+CV)` |
| AChE inhibited-pool ODE | n/a | Appendix II / Figure 2 |

## Units (dimensional check)

Amounts are in mg, concentrations mg/L, volumes L, flows L/h, time h; enzyme
pools are dimensionless fractions of baseline activity. The MM hydrolysis term
`Vmax [mg/h] * cv [mg/L] / (Km [mg/L] + cv [mg/L])` has units mg/h, matching
`d/dt(amount) [mg/h]`. The enzyme-driving concentration is converted to uM for
the bimolecular rate: `dfp_uM = C [mg/L] * 1000 / mw [g/mol]`, so
`ki [1/uM/h] * dfp_uM [uM] * free [-]` has units 1/h, matching
`d/dt(free) [1/h]`. DFP molecular weight is 184.15 g/mol (Appendix I uses
184 mg/mmole).

# Mouse: DFP pharmacokinetics (replicates Figure 3)

Martin (1974) injected male mice with 1 mg DFP/kg iv (tail vein) and measured
free DFP in plasma and brain. The dose enters the venous blood compartment.

```{r mouse-pk}
bw_mouse <- mUi$theta[["bw"]]
dose_mouse <- 1 * bw_mouse # 1 mg/kg iv

ev_pk <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mouse, cmt = "a_venous", time = 0) |>
  rxode2::et(c(seq(0, 0.5, length.out = 300), seq(0.6, 30, length.out = 200)))
pk <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mUi, ev_pk, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))

pk_long <- pk |>
  dplyr::transmute(time_min = time * 60, Plasma = Cc, Brain = Cbrain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "dfp")

ggplot(dplyr::filter(pk_long, time_min <= 3), aes(time_min, dfp, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (minutes)", y = "DFP (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Mouse DFP after 1 mg/kg iv (first 3 min)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a,b of Gearhart 1994 (plasma and brain DFP)."
  )
```

Free DFP disappears from plasma within about a minute (Figure 3a) and brain DFP
peaks below 2 mg/L and falls over the next few minutes (Figure 3b,d), driven by
the very high blood and tissue A-esterase activity:

```{r mouse-pk-features}
peak_brain <- max(pk$Cbrain)
t_detect_plasma <- pk$time[pk$Cc > 0.1][length(pk$time[pk$Cc > 0.1])] * 60
peak_brain
t_detect_plasma
# Brain DFP peak is a small-molar quantity (Figure 3b shows a peak below ~2 mg/L)
stopifnot(peak_brain > 0.2, peak_brain < 2.5)
# Plasma DFP has largely disappeared within a couple of minutes (Figure 3a)
stopifnot(t_detect_plasma < 2)
```

# Mouse: AChE inhibition (replicates Figures 4 and 5)

The same 1 mg/kg iv dose is followed out to 7 days to track plasma and brain
AChE activity. Gearhart report the nadir of AChE within about 1 min in plasma
and about 5 min in brain, and that brain AChE 7 days after a single injection
had recovered only to about 80% of control (Figure 5c), while plasma recovered
toward 100% within about 3.75 days.

```{r mouse-ache}
ev_pd <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_mouse, cmt = "a_venous", time = 0) |>
  rxode2::et(c(seq(0, 1, length.out = 200), seq(1.5, 192, length.out = 400)))
pd <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mUi, ev_pd, atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-9))

ache_long <- pd |>
  dplyr::transmute(time_h = time, Plasma = ache_plasma, Brain = ache_brain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "activity")

ggplot(ache_long, aes(time_h, activity, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (hours)", y = "AChE activity (fraction of control)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Mouse AChE after 1 mg/kg iv DFP",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 4 (plasma) and 5 (brain) of Gearhart 1994."
  )
```

```{r mouse-ache-features}
nadir_plasma <- min(pd$ache_plasma)
nadir_brain <- min(pd$ache_brain)
brain_7d <- approx(pd$time, pd$ache_brain, 168)$y
plasma_90h <- approx(pd$time, pd$ache_plasma, 90)$y
round(c(nadir_plasma = nadir_plasma, nadir_brain = nadir_brain,
        brain_7d = brain_7d, plasma_90h = plasma_90h), 3)

# Both enzymes are strongly inhibited at the nadir (Figures 4a, 5a show nadirs
# well below half of control).
stopifnot(nadir_plasma < 0.3, nadir_brain < 0.45)
# Brain AChE recovers slowly; at 7 days it is still well below control but has
# recovered substantially (Gearhart: ~80% of control at 7 days, Figure 5c).
stopifnot(brain_7d > 0.65, brain_7d < 0.95)
# Plasma AChE recovers faster than brain (Gearhart: ~100% within ~3.75 days).
stopifnot(plasma_90h > brain_7d)
```

# Mass balance

The model conserves DFP mass: the administered dose equals the amount still in
the body plus the cumulative amount hydrolysed by A-esterase plus the cumulative
amount exhaled.

```{r mass-balance}
comps <- c(
  "depot", "a_venous", "a_arterial", "a_brain", "a_liver", "a_kidney",
  "a_rich", "a_fat", "a_slow", "a_diaphragm"
)
end <- pd[nrow(pd), ]
recovered <- sum(as.numeric(end[comps])) + end$a_hydrolyzed + end$a_exhaled
rel_err <- (recovered - dose_mouse) / dose_mouse
round(c(dose = dose_mouse, recovered = recovered, rel_err = rel_err), 8)
stopifnot(abs(rel_err) < 1e-4)
```

# Baseline hold

With no dose, all AChE pools sit at the pre-exposure baseline (activity = 1)
indefinitely: zero-order synthesis exactly balances first-order degradation.

```{r baseline}
ev0 <- rxode2::et(amt = 0, cmt = "a_venous", time = 0) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 240, length.out = 200))
s0 <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mUi, ev0))
range(s0$ache_brain)
range(s0$ache_plasma)
stopifnot(all(abs(s0$ache_brain - 1) < 1e-6), all(abs(s0$ache_plasma - 1) < 1e-6))
```

# Rat: repeated subcutaneous dosing (Figures 6 and 7)

Traina & Serpietri (1984) and Michalek et al. (1982) gave male Wistar rats DFP
sc every second day for 22 days (first dose 1.1 mg/kg, then 0.7 mg/kg) and
followed plasma and brain AChE. The sc absorption rate was visually optimised by
the authors but not tabulated, so a placeholder first-order rate is used here
(see Assumptions); the simulation reproduces the qualitative pattern - a rapid
fall during dosing to a sustained low plateau, then recovery after dosing stops.

```{r rat-repeat}
bw_rat <- rUi$theta[["bw"]]
ev_rat <- rxode2::et(amt = 1.1 * bw_rat, cmt = "depot", time = 0)
for (d in seq(2, 22, by = 2)) {
  ev_rat <- rxode2::et(ev_rat, amt = 0.7 * bw_rat, cmt = "depot", time = d * 24)
}
ev_rat <- rxode2::et(ev_rat, seq(0, 40 * 24, length.out = 1500))
rt <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rUi, ev_rat, atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-9))

rt |>
  dplyr::transmute(day = time / 24, Plasma = ache_plasma, Brain = ache_brain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Plasma, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "activity") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, activity, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 22, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "AChE activity (fraction of control)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Rat AChE during and after 22 days of repeated sc DFP",
    caption = "Replicates Figures 6 (plasma) and 7 (brain) of Gearhart 1994."
  )
```

```{r rat-features}
# During dosing both enzymes are driven to a sustained low plateau; after
# dosing stops (day 22) they recover toward control.
nadir_rat_brain <- min(rt$ache_brain)
end_rat_brain <- approx(rt$time, rt$ache_brain, 40 * 24)$y
round(c(nadir_rat_brain = nadir_rat_brain, end_rat_brain = end_rat_brain), 3)
stopifnot(nadir_rat_brain < 0.6, end_rat_brain > nadir_rat_brain + 0.3)
```

# Human: dose-response at 24 h (Figure 8)

Grob et al. (1947) gave volunteers a single im injection of DFP (33 ug/kg, and
acute doses from 10 to 54 ug/kg) and measured red-blood-cell AChE. The model's
blood AChE output is compared against RBC-AChE (plasma butyrylcholinesterase,
also shown in Figure 8, is not modelled - see Assumptions). As for the rat, the
im absorption rate is a placeholder, so the comparison here is the dose-ordering
of maximal inhibition rather than the exact timing.

```{r human-dr}
bw_human <- hUi$theta[["bw"]]
doses_ugkg <- c(10, 33, 54)
hr <- lapply(doses_ugkg, function(d) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = d / 1000 * bw_human, cmt = "depot", time = 0) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 48, length.out = 600))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(hUi, ev, atol = 1e-9, rtol = 1e-9))
  data.frame(dose_ugkg = d, nadir_rbc_ache = min(s$ache_plasma))
})
hr <- do.call(rbind, hr)
hr |>
  dplyr::rename("DFP dose (ug/kg)" = dose_ugkg, "RBC-AChE nadir (fraction of control)" = nadir_rbc_ache) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Human RBC-AChE maximal inhibition by im DFP dose (Figure 8).")

# Higher doses give deeper RBC-AChE inhibition (lower nadir).
stopifnot(all(diff(hr$nadir_rbc_ache) < 0))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Full text is scanned page images.** The article's model parameters are
  distributed as scanned page images rather than machine-readable text; the
  maintainers read every value directly from Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 and recorded
  the table location in each `ini()` comment.
- **sc/im absorption rate not reported.** The rate of DFP absorption after sc
  (rat) and im (human) injection was described as visually optimised and
  particularly influential on the initial fall in AChE, but no numeric value is
  tabulated. A placeholder first-order rate (`ka = 1 /h`, `lka = 0`) is carried
  so the extravascular route is functional; it is clearly labelled NOT REPORTED
  in each file. The rat and human figure reproductions therefore validate the
  magnitude and dose-ordering of inhibition, not the exact nadir timing (which
  this rate governs). The mouse validation uses iv dosing and does not depend on
  it.
- **Butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) and carboxylesterase (CaE) not modelled.** The
  paper also tracks plasma BChE (Figure 8) and CaE as DFP targets, with
  bimolecular rate constants in Table 1, but Table 3's synthesis, degradation,
  regeneration and aging constants are given only for AChE. BChE/CaE turnover is
  therefore not reproducible from the tables and these enzymes are omitted; only
  AChE (brain and blood) is modelled.
- **Covalent DFP-esterase sink on DFP mass balance omitted.** Appendix II writes
  a bimolecular DFP-esterase binding term in the DFP mass balance, but the
  Discussion states the low molar concentration of the esterases makes this sink
  negligible for DFP kinetics. It is omitted from the DFP ODEs (the enzyme pools
  are still driven by local DFP), so DFP mass balance closes on hydrolysis plus
  exhalation.
- **Lung as a steady-state gas exchanger.** No lung:blood partition coefficient
  is reported, so the lung is encoded as the standard algebraic steady-state
  gas-exchange relationship (blood:air partition only) rather than as a
  distribution compartment; for the injection scenarios validated here this
  contributes only a small pulmonary exhalation loss.
- **Deterministic.** The publication reports no IIV and no residual error; the
  models carry none.
- **Correction notices.** No erratum or correction notice for this article was
  found as of 2026-11-18.
```
